_comment_student: The English and Tamil cells use `arun`, who speaks both. The Mandarin cells cannot: his `speaks` names Tamil and English, so the prompt would order him to write in a language it also says he does not have. They use `li` instead, a profile pinned to arun's age and grade so the swap costs only name, home language and region. That is a real confound and the Mandarin column is not a pure language contrast against the other two - it is the tightest coherent one available without re-running English and Tamil on a fourth profile.
_comment: Tutor-model comparison. Four tutors x three languages, twelve cells. Everything else is pinned: same student model, same student profile, same topic, same level (`struggling`), one run each, 15 turns per speaker (30 messages). So the only things that differ between cells are the tutor model and the language, and the English/Tamil pair for a given tutor differs in language alone. `struggling` is the level to compare tutors on - `robust` belief plus `slow` change rate means a tutor has to actually work, where `advanced` reaches the answer almost regardless of who is teaching.
_comment_reasoning: `tutor_reasoning` is null, not "none", because three of the four tutors do not accept the parameter at all: llama-4-maverick and grok-4.3 raise UnsupportedParamsError from litellm and claude-sonnet-5 errors inside it. Null means the parameter is not sent and the provider default applies. gemini-3.5-flash is the exception and would accept "none", but it is deliberately left at null too - setting it on one tutor and not the others would make that cell differ in a second way, and gemini-3 cannot disable thinking regardless (see `catalog.reasoning_not_honoured`). So no cell here is a no-reasoning run: grok-4.3 was measured spending 207 reasoning tokens on a two-word reply with no knob to turn it off. `reasoning_tokens_spent` in session_end is the auditable number. The student keeps "none", which gemini-3.1-pro-preview accepts and then ignores.
